def dsl5(I):
    # -------------------------------------------------
    # Strategy 5 – Relational row replication
    # -------------------------------------------------
    # For every row that contains a 5 in column 0, build a copy of that
    # row with the leading cell set to 0.  Then repeat those copies
    # (cycling) until the grid is filled, finally trimming excess zeros.
    anchor           = ofcolor(I, 5)                     # positions of colour 5
    row_indices      = { r for r,_ in anchor }           # rows that have a 5
    # whole rows of those indices
    rows_patch       = mapply(lambda d: shift(anchor, (0, d)),
                              interval(ZERO, width(I), ONE))
    cleared_anchor   = recolor(0, anchor)
    I0               = paint(I, cleared_anchor)          # colour 5 → 0
    pattern_rows     = subgrid(rows_patch, I0)           # rows with left cell 0

    # how many copies are needed to fill the empty part?
    empty_rows       = subtract(height(I),
                                 add(valmax({ r for r,_ in ofcolor(I,0) },
                                           lambda x: x), ONE))
    repeat_count     = divide(empty_rows, size(row_indices))

    # build the repeated block (cycling the pattern rows)
    cycle_one        = lambda g: vconcat(g, pattern_rows)
    repeated_block   = power(cycle_one,
                             subtract(repeat_count, ONE))(pattern_rows)

    # keep the original non‑empty part and attach the repeated block
    nz               = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))
    nz_rows_patch    = mapply(lambda d: shift(nz, (0, d)),
                              interval(ZERO, width(I), ONE))
    base             = subgrid(nz_rows_patch, I)

    O = vconcat(base, repeated_block)
    O = trim(O)                                         # drop leftover zeros
    return O
```

def dsl1(I):
    # -------------------------------------------------
    # Strategy 1 – Row‑wise replication (clear‑anchor version)
    # -------------------------------------------------
    # 1.  Anchor rows = rows that contain colour 5 in column 0.
    anchor       = ofcolor(I, 5)                                 # {(r,0)}
    rows_patch   = mapply(lambda d: shift(anchor, (0, d)),
                         interval(ZERO, width(I), ONE))          # whole rows
    # 2.  Clear the leading 5 in those rows.
    cleared      = recolor(0, anchor)
    I0           = paint(I, cleared)                             # colour 5 → 0
    pattern      = subgrid(rows_patch, I0)                       # rows without leading 5
    # 3.  How many empty rows are below the lowest non‑zero cell ?
    nz           = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))        # all non‑zero cells
    max_nz_row   = valmax(nz, lambda p: p[0])                   # bottom row index
    empty_rows   = subtract(height(I), add(max_nz_row, ONE))
    # 4.  Number of rows that belong to the pattern.
    pattern_rows = size({ r for r,_ in anchor })
    repeat_cnt   = divide(empty_rows, pattern_rows)             # whole blocks to add
    # 5.  Build the repeated block (repeat_cnt copies of *pattern*).
    repeat_one   = lambda g: vconcat(g, pattern)
    repeat_block = branch(greater(repeat_cnt, ONE),
                         power(repeat_one, subtract(repeat_cnt, ONE))(pattern),
                         pattern)
    # 6.  Keep the original non‑empty part (crop to the bbox of nz).
    base         = subgrid(backdrop(nz), I)
    # 7.  Append the repeated block and trim trailing zero rows.
    O = trim(vconcat(base, repeat_block))
    return O

    # -------------------------------------------------
    # Strategy 2 – Crop → vertical‑mirror only the anchor rows
    # -------------------------------------------------
    # 1.  Crop to the tight bounding box of all non‑zero cells.
    nz        = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))

    rows_pat  = mapply(lambda d: shift(anchor, (0, d)),

    pat_rows  = subgrid(rows_pat, core0)        # pattern rows

    mirror    = vmirror(pat_rows)
    # 4.  Stack the original core with the mirrored pattern and trim.
    O = trim(vconcat(core, mirror))
    return O

    # Strategy 3 – Colour‑filtering then full duplication
    # -------------------------------------------------
    # 1.  Remove colour 5 (set to 0) everywhere.

    dup_block = branch(greater(repeats, ONE),
                      power(dup_one, subtract(repeats, ONE))(I0),
                      I0)
    O = trim(dup_block)
    return O

def dsl2(I):
    # ----- core: crop‑then‑repeat (uses crop instead of subgrid/backdrop) -----
    nz        = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))
    core      = crop(I, (ZERO, ZERO), (height(I), width(I)))        # full grid (no trim)
    core_bbox = backdrop(nz)                                       # bbox of non‑zero part
    core_cropped = subgrid(core_bbox, I)                          # tight crop of original
    anchor    = ofcolor(core_cropped, 5)
    rows_patch = mapply(lambda d: shift(anchor, (0, d)),
                       interval(ZERO, width(core_cropped), ONE))
    cleared   = recolor(0, anchor)
    core0     = paint(core_cropped, cleared)                       # clear leading 5 in the crop
    pattern   = subgrid(rows_patch, core0)                         # pattern rows (cleared)
    max_nz   = valmax(nz, lambda p: p[0])
    empty    = subtract(height(I), add(max_nz, ONE))
    repeat   = divide(empty, size({ r for r,_ in anchor }))
    repeat_one = lambda g: vconcat(g, pattern)
    repeated   = branch(greater(repeat, ONE),
                       power(repeat_one, subtract(repeat, ONE))(pattern),
                       pattern)
    O = trim(vconcat(core_cropped, repeated))
    return O
```

def dsl3(I):
    # ----- core: colour‑filtering + explicit move (object‑extraction style) -----
    anchor   = ofcolor(I, 5)                                    # cells with colour 5
    rows_ids = { r for r,_ in anchor }                           # rows that carry a 5
    rows_patch = mapply(lambda d: shift(anchor, (0, d)),
                        interval(ZERO, width(I), ONE))
    cleared   = recolor(0, anchor)
    I0        = paint(I, cleared)                               # clear leading 5
    pattern   = subgrid(rows_patch, I0)                          # pattern rows (cleared)

    nz        = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))
    max_nz    = valmax(nz, lambda p: p[0])
    empty     = subtract(height(I), add(max_nz, ONE))
    repeat_cnt = divide(empty, size(rows_ids))

    # shift the pattern down repeatedly and concatenate the copies
    shift_one = lambda g: vconcat(g, pattern)
    repeated  = branch(greater(repeat_cnt, ONE),
                     power(shift_one, subtract(repeat_cnt, ONE))(pattern),
                     pattern)

    base = subgrid(backdrop(nz), I)                            # original non‑zero part
    O = trim(vconcat(base, repeated))
    return O

def dsl1(I):
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1️⃣  Global – crop the “anchor” rows, clear the leading 5 and tile them
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    anchor      = ofcolor(I, 5)                                            # {(r,0)}
    rows_set    = { r for r,_ in anchor }                                 # set of anchor rows
    rows_patch  = mapply(lambda d: shift(anchor, (0, d)),
                        interval(ZERO, width(I), ONE)                     # whole anchor rows
    cleared     = recolor(0, anchor)                                       # 5 → 0 inside the block
    I0          = paint(I, cleared)                                        # grid with leading 5 cleared
    pattern_g   = subgrid(rows_patch, I0)                                   # pattern (cleared)

    # ----- how many copies fit in the empty area below the data ? ----------
    nz          = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))                   # all non‑zero cells
    max_nz_row  = valmax(nz, lambda p: p[0])                               # lowest occupied row
    empty_rows  = subtract(height(I), add(max_nz_row, ONE))                 # rows of pure 0 under the data
    repeat_cnt  = divide(empty_rows, size(rows_set))                       # how many pattern blocks fit

    # ----- build the repeated block by shifting the pattern down ----------------
    h           = size(rows_set)                                           # height of one block
    pat_obj     = asobject(pattern_g)                                      # pattern as an object
    shifts      = mapply(lambda i: shift(pat_obj,
                                         (multiply(add(i, ONE), h), ZERO)),
                        interval(ZERO, repeat_cnt, ONE))                # i = 0 … repeat_cnt‑1,
                                                                       # first copy placed just below the original
    repeated    = merge(shifts)                                            # all shifted copies together

    # ----- keep the original picture (including the leading 5) ----------------
    base        = subgrid(backdrop(nz), I)                                 # original non‑zero part
    O           = trim(paint(base, repeated))                             # overlay copies and trim trailing zeros
    return O

def dsl3(I):
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3️⃣  Colour‑filtering – first remove colour 5 everywhere, then repeat
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # remove all 5s globally (keeps the shape of the pattern)
    cleared_all = recolor(0, ofcolor(I, 5))
    I_no5       = paint(I, cleared_all)

    # rows that originally contained a 5 (they are now rows with any non‑zero)

    rows_patch  = mapply(lambda d: shift(ofcolor(I, 5), (0, d)),
                        interval(ZERO, width(I), ONE))
    pattern_g   = subgrid(rows_patch,
                         paint(I, recolor(0, ofcolor(I, 5))))          # pattern with 5 cleared

    # how many full copies fit below the existing structure ?
    nz          = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))
    max_nz_row  = valmax(nz, lambda p: p[0])

                                         (multiply(add(i, ONE), h), ZERO)),
                         interval(ZERO, repeat_cnt, ONE))
    tiled       = merge(shifted)

    base        = subgrid(backdrop(nz), I)
    O           = trim(paint(base, tiled))
    return O

def dsl4(I):
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4️⃣  Geometric – use vertical mirroring to obtain the “filled” block
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    anchor      = ofcolor(I, 5)
    rows_set    = { r for r,_ in anchor }
    rows_patch  = mapply(lambda d: shift(anchor, (0, d)),
                        interval(ZERO, width(I), ONE))
    cleared     = recolor(0, anchor)
    I0          = paint(I, cleared)
    pattern_g   = subgrid(rows_patch, I0)          # pattern without leading 5

    # mirror the pattern vertically and stack it – this yields a block that can
    # be repeated without the leading 5 (the mirror creates the missing rows)
    mirrored    = vmirror(pattern_g)
    doubled_g   = vconcat(pattern_g, mirrored)     # one full period (original + mirror)

    # how many whole periods fit in the empty space ?
    nz          = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))
    max_nz_row  = valmax(nz, lambda p: p[0])
    empty_rows  = subtract(height(I), add(max_nz_row, ONE))
    period_h    = height(doubled_g)
    repeat_cnt  = divide(empty_rows, period_h)

    # repeat the doubled block the required number of times
    repeat_one  = lambda g: vconcat(g, doubled_g)
    repeated_g  = branch(greater(repeat_cnt, ONE),
                         power(repeat_one, subtract(repeat_cnt, ONE))(doubled_g),
                         doubled_g)

    base        = subgrid(backdrop(nz), I)
    O           = trim(vconcat(base, repeated_g))
    return O
```

    tiled_obj   = merge(shifted_objs)

    base_grid   = subgrid(backdrop(nz), I)
    O           = trim(paint(base_grid, tiled_obj))

    tiled       = merge(shifted)

def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC – build a period by mirroring the cleared rows and tile it
    anchor      = ofcolor(I, 5)
    rows_set    = { r for r,_ in anchor }
    rows_patch  = mapply(lambda d: shift(anchor, (0, d)),
                         interval(ZERO, width(I), ONE))
    cleared     = recolor(0, anchor)
    I0          = paint(I, cleared)
    pattern_g   = subgrid(rows_patch, I0)                                 # cleared rows

    # create one period by mirroring vertically and concatenating
    mirrored    = vmirror(pattern_g)
    period_g    = vconcat(pattern_g, mirrored)                           # one full period

    # repeat the period as many times as fits
    nz          = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))
    max_nz_row  = valmax(nz, lambda p: p[0])
    empty_rows  = subtract(height(I), add(max_nz_row, ONE))
    period_h    = height(period_g)
    repeat_cnt  = divide(empty_rows, period_h)

    period_obj  = asobject(period_g)
    shifted     = mapply(lambda i: shift(period_obj,
                                         (multiply(add(i, ONE), period_h), ZERO)),
                         interval(ZERO, repeat_cnt, ONE))
    tiled_obj   = merge(shifted)

    base        = subgrid(backdrop(nz), I)
    O           = trim(paint(base, tiled_obj))
    return O

def dsl1(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION – rows that contain a 5 are cleared and tiled vertically
    anchor      = ofcolor(I, 5)                                            # cells with colour 5
    rows_set    = { r for r,_ in anchor }                                   # rows that hold a 5
    rows_cells  = product(rows_set, interval(ZERO, width(I), ONE))          # full‑width cells of those rows
    cleared     = recolor(0, anchor)                                        # erase the 5s
    I0          = paint(I, cleared)                                         # grid with the block cleared
    pattern_g   = subgrid(rows_cells, I0)                                   # cleared rows as a grid
    pattern_o   = asobject(pattern_g)                                       # object representation

    nz          = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))                    # all non‑zero cells in the original
    max_nz_row = valmax(nz, lambda p: p[0])                                # lowest occupied row
    empty_rows  = subtract(height(I), add(max_nz_row, ONE))                 # rows still empty at the bottom
    repeat_cnt  = divide(empty_rows, size(rows_set))                       # how many full copies fit

    offsets = mapply(lambda i: astuple(multiply(add(i, ONE), size(rows_set)),
                                      ZERO),
                    interval(ZERO, repeat_cnt, ONE))
    shifted = mapply(lambda off: shift(pattern_o, off), offsets)           # shifted copies
    tiled   = merge(shifted)                                                # union of all copies

    base   = subgrid(backdrop(nz), I)                                       # keep original picture
    O      = trim(paint(base, tiled))                                       # overlay the tiled block
    return O

    anchor      = ofcolor(I, 5)

    pattern_g   = subgrid(rows_cells, I0)                                    # cleared rows as a grid
    pattern_o   = asobject(pattern_g)

    repeat_cnt  = divide(empty_rows, size(rows_set))

                                   astuple(multiply(add(i, ONE), size(rows_set)),
                                           ZERO)),
                   interval(ZERO, repeat_cnt, ONE))
    tiled   = merge(copies)

    base   = subgrid(backdrop(nz), I)
    O      = trim(paint(base, tiled))
    return O

def dsl3(I):
    # GEOMETRIC – treat the cleared rows as a period and repeat it using vupscale
    anchor      = ofcolor(I, 5)
    rows_set    = { r for r,_ in anchor }
    rows_cells  = product(rows_set, interval(ZERO, width(I), ONE))

    I0          = paint(I, recolor(0, anchor))
    period_g    = subgrid(rows_cells, I0)                                   # period to repeat
    period_h    = height(period_g)

    nz          = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))
    max_nz_row = valmax(nz, lambda p: p[0])
    empty_rows  = subtract(height(I), add(max_nz_row, ONE))
    repeat_cnt  = divide(empty_rows, period_h)

    # repeat the period vertically (including the original copy)
    repeated_g  = vupscale(period_g, add(repeat_cnt, ONE))

    # discard the first copy (the original rows) and keep only the newly created part
    extra_g     = subgrid(product(interval(period_h, height(repeated_g), ONE),
                         interval(ZERO, width(I), ONE)),
                         repeated_g)

    O = paint(I, asobject(extra_g))
    return O

def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL EXTRACTOR
    # 1.  Treat every horizontal neighbour pair as an object of width 2.
    # 2.  Count how many times each colour‑pair occurs (colorcount on the pair‑object).
    # 3.  Pick the two most frequent pairs, turn each into a two‑digit integer,
    #     and output them as a 2 × 1 grid.
    pairs = {tuple(sorted([index(I, (r, c)), index(I, (r, c+1))])
              for r in range(len(I))
              for c in range(len(I[0]) - 1))}
    # helper: frequency of each pair (as a frozenset so it can be a dict key)
    freq = {p: colorcount(I, p[0]) + colorcount(I, p[1]) for p in pairs}
    top2 = list(sorted(freq.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:2])
    nums = tuple(add(multiply(p[0][0], 10), p[0][1]) for p in top2)
    O = ((nums[0],), (nums[1],))
    return O

def dsl3(I):
    # COLOR‑FILTERING STRATEGY
    # 1.  Determine the two most common colours in the whole grid.
    # 2.  Scan each row left‑to‑right and keep the first occurrence where those two colours appear consecutively.
    # 3.  Convert the two digits to a number and output it twice.
    most = list(mostcommon(palette(I)))[:2]
    a, b = most[0], most[1]
    def first_adjacent(row):

                     if row[i] == a and row[i+1] == b), (a, b))
    pair = first_adjacent(I[0])
    num = add(multiply(pair[0], 10), pair[1])
    O = ((num,), (num,))
    return O

def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL REASONING
    # 1.  Find the most common adjacent colour pair (using manhattan on neighbour cells).
    # 2.  Record the two digits, make the two‑digit number.
    # 3.  Return this number in a 2 × 1 grid.
    neighbours = [(r, c) for r in range(len(I)) for c in range(len(I[0]) - 1)]
    pair_counts = {}
    for p in neighbours:
        d1 = index(I, p)
        d2 = index(I, (p[0], p[1]+1))
        pair = (d1, d2)
        pair_counts[pair] = pair_counts.get(pair, 0) + 1
    top_pair = max(pair_counts.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])[0]
    num = add(multiply(top_pair[0], 10), top_pair[1])
    O = ((num,), (num,))
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – treat each colour region as an object, count left‑adjacent colour pairs.
    objs   = objects(I, False, False, True)            # connected colour objects
    cols   = palette(I)
    pairs  = product(cols, cols)
    distinct= mfilter(pairs, lambda p: p[0] != p[1])
    # for a colour a, collect all cells belonging to objects of colour a
    cells_a = lambda c: apply(lambda o: o,           # identity – objects are already sets of cells
                               colorfilter(objs, c))
    # union of all those cell‑sets
    union_a = lambda c: combine(apply(lambda o: o, cells_a(c)), initset())
    left_of = lambda a, b: size(intersection(
                 union_a(a),
                 shift(union_a(b), LEFT)))
    top1    = argmax(distinct, lambda p: left_of(p[0], p[1]))
    top2    = argmax(difference(distinct, initset(top1)),
                     lambda p: left_of(p[0], p[1]))
    n1 = add(multiply(top1[0], 10), top1[1])
    n2 = add(multiply(top2[0], 10), top2[1])
    O = ((n1,), (n2,))
    return O
```

    # GEOMETRIC – analyse only the first horizontal repetition period.
    per      = hperiod(I)                                 # width of the fundamental repeat
    slice    = hsplit(I, per)[0]                          # first period slice
    colors   = palette(slice)
    left_of = lambda a, b: size(intersection(ofcolor(slice, a),
                                            shift(ofcolor(slice, b), LEFT)))

    pairs    = mfilter(product(colors, colors), lambda p: p[0] != p[1])
    best1    = argmax(pairs, lambda p: left_of(p[0], p[1]))
    best2    = argmax(difference(pairs, initset(best1)),
                      lambda p: left_of(p[0], p[1]))

    n1 = add(multiply(best1[0], 10), best1[1])
    n2 = add(multiply(best2[0], 10), best2[1])
    return ((n1,), (n2,))

def dsl5(I):
    # REVERSED – count how many b‑cells lie immediately to the right of a‑cells
    # (i.e. the opposite direction) and then output the pair in original order.
    colours = palette(I)

    right_of = lambda a, b: size(
                 intersection(
                     shift(ofcolor(I, a), RIGHT),
                     ofcolor(I, b)))

    pairs   = mfilter(product(colours, colours),
                     lambda p: p[0] != p[1])

    max1    = valmax(pairs, lambda p: right_of(p[0], p[1]))
    best1   = extract(pairs,
                     lambda p: right_of(p[0], p[1]) == max1)

    pairs2  = difference(pairs, initset(best1))
    max2    = valmax(pairs2, lambda p: right_of(p[0], p[1]))
    best2   = extract(pairs2,
                     lambda p: right_of(p[0], p[1]) == max2)

    # swap back to original left‑right orientation
    n1 = add(multiply(best1[1], 10), best1[0])
    n2 = add(multiply(best2[1], 10), best2[0])
    return ((n1,), (n2,))
```
